name: Carrion Defense Works Miasma Projector MP-5 'Plague Bearer'
description: A pressurized chemical dispersal weapon that launches canisters of Carrion's proprietary incapacitant compound — a viscous aerosol that adheres to surfaces and continues to off-gas for up to six hours. The compound causes severe mucous membrane irritation, temporary blindness, and uncontrollable retching in unprotected targets. It is technically classified as non-lethal, though confined-space deployment has resulted in documented fatalities from asphyxiation. The persistent nature of the compound makes it particularly effective for area denial.
legality: Licensed — riot control and area denial; Restricted — civilian
specifications:
canister range: 40-80 meters (launched)
area of effect: 15 meter radius per canister
persistence: 4-6 hours on surfaces
magazine: 6 canisters
weight: 4.1 kg loaded
compound: Carrion CDW-Incap7 viscous aerosol
countermeasure: Filtered rebreather with ocular seal required
story_hooks: Someone deployed Miasma canisters in a sealed residential ventilation system in Tier 2 — forty people hospitalized, three dead, and the canisters had their serial numbers chemically erased.
A Carrion chemist has developed a variant that selectively affects people based on their blood chemistry — it only incapacitates targets with specific pharmaceutical markers.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, industrial dispersal weapon with a pronounced barrel assembly and bulbous pressure chamber. Resembles a hybrid between a riot launcher and a pressurized pesticide applicator — all hard angles and utilitarian bulk. The silhouette reads as deliberately ominous: wide stance, asymmetrical weight distribution, mechanical. No grace; pure function.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 68 cm | Barrel assembly: 32 cm | Pressure chamber diameter: 11 cm | Magazine depth: 14 cm | Width at grip: 8.5 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-heavy when unloaded (4.1 kg fully loaded). The weight shifts forward toward the barrel, demanding two-handed control. Balanced on the magazine well, it feels purposeful and grounded — no quick-draw weapon, but stable and authoritative in sustained aim.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced injection-molded polymer frame with steel pressure chamber lining. Aluminum alloy mounting rail system. Stainless steel nozzle array and canister indexing mechanism.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial grey-black polymer body with visible stress-relief ribbing. Steel pressure chamber shows brushed finish with micro-oxidation scarring from repeated pressurization cycles. Nozzle tips feature burnt bronze patina from off-gassing residue exposure.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey primary body | Charcoal black ribbed grip zones | Burnt copper/bronze nozzle accents | Red pressure-release valve cap (safety indicator)
physical_description.grip_texture: Deeply ribbed textured polymer with aggressive ergonomic molding. Two-point grip area: side-mounted assist handle wrapped in degraded rubberized coating. Main grip is almost sandpaper-rough for wet/gloved use in riot conditions.
distinctive_features: Dual pressure gauges mounted on chamber flank (red/amber/green threat-level indicators)
Spring-loaded canister indexing carousel with numeric load-state engraving (1-6)
Vented exhaust ports along barrel with visible carbonized residue buildup
Prominent safety interlocks with manual mechanical override (corroded brass housing)
Manufacturer serial plate stamped directly into polymer body — faded but legible
Custom wear marks and chemical etching on nozzle tip from persistent compound exposure
Integrated mounting rail (Picatinny) scarred and salt-corroded from field deployment
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS logo embossed on left side of pressure chamber | Model designation 'MP-5' stamped above grip | 'PLAGUE BEARER' variant tag laser-etched on barrel shroud | Serial number and certification code on chamber flank | Hazmat/corrosive material warning symbols on both sides of grip
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn and chemically stained. Polymer body shows stress crazing in high-impact areas. Nozzle assembly exhibits patina from repeated off-gassing events. Pressure gauges often smudged or fogged. Magazine carousel mechanism loose from wear. This is not a pristine asset — it's a working tool showing honest battle scars.
